criteria.text: Identifies that the basket in SPA Section 9.4 ($200,000) operates as a deductible (Seller liable only for the excess), not a tipping basket, and explains that this is less favourable to the Buyer.
Calculates the Earn-out Payment as $3,900,000 (3 x ($7,800,000 - $6,500,000), subject to the $5,000,000 cap) and identifies that the Seller's figure of $4,500,000 is wrong.

Identifies the conflict between the 30-day claim notice period in SPA Section 9.7 and the 60-day period in Escrow Clause 5.2, and recommends the Buyer works to the shorter 30-day period or aligns the documents.
Calculates the working capital shortfall as $910,000 and the adjusted Purchase Price as $19,090,000, identifying that the Seller's funds flow figure of $18,180,000 is wrong.

Identifies that the MAC carve-outs (general economic, industry-wide and pandemic changes) contain no 'disproportionate effect' exception, so the Buyer bears those risks even where the Company is disproportionately affected, and recommends adding one.
Explains how 'material adverse effect' could be read narrowly or broadly and what each reading means for the Buyer's walk-away right.
Shows the earn-out arithmetic and flags the discrepancy between $3,900,000 and the Seller's $4,500,000.
Gives a pinpoint citation (document name and section/clause number) for every issue or finding.
